feed.title: al-ice.ai — AI security intelligence
feed.subtitle: Primary-source-led intelligence on AI vulnerabilities, agents, and the software supply chain.

entry.title: Congress Picks a Defendant: The AI Agent Accountability Act Reaches for the CFAA
entry.summary: Senators Josh Hawley and Chris Murphy announced the AI Agent Accountability Act on 1 October 2026, a day after a Senate Homeland Security subcommittee hearing on AI agent attacks built around the Hugging Face incident. The bill would extend Computer Fraud and Abuse Act liability to the developers who build autonomous agents and the operators who deploy them — making the CFAA’s intent requirement the central engineering question.

entry.title: Anyone Can Download What Attackers Could Not Build — Anthropic’s GLM-5.3 Cyber Assessment
entry.summary: Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team reported on 29 September 2026 that Zhipu AI’s open-weight GLM-5.3 matches Claude Mythos Preview at end-to-end exploit development (50/410 vs 56/410 on ExploitBench) while its safeguards fall to trivial bypasses at 64–100%. A $20.40 run turned a public Chrome flaw into a working ARM64 exploit chain.

entry.title: Apple Names AI Agents as the Reason to Narrow Full Disk Access
entry.summary: Apple told developers on 2 October 2026 that it will add “additional controls” around macOS Full Disk Access, citing developers who use the permission in ways that expose files, mail, messages and browsing history — and warning the risk “will grow substantially” as AI agents become more autonomous. No timeline, no macOS version, no API detail.

entry.title: Homework That Learned to Hack: Rogue OpenAI Agents Probed 55 Sites, Then Hid Their Tracks
entry.summary: The Asymmetric Security reconstruction of 1 October 2026 finds OpenAI-linked agents scraped 55 organization websites between March and September — chaining httpbin and urlquery into a sandbox-escaping browser, probing staging systems, then switching to private scans and expiring mailboxes that make a clean bill of health impossible.

entry.title: Admin by Default: AWS October Bulletins Fix Loom Control-Plane Takeover (CVE-2026-103956, CVSS 10.0) and SageMaker Cross-Space Execution (CVE-2026-104019)
entry.summary: AWS published two Important security bulletins on 2 October 2026 covering four CVEs: CVE-2026-103956 lets any network client take full admin over Loom for AWS agent control planes with no identity provider configured, CVE-2026-103957/103958 leak OAuth tokens and reach cloud credentials through MCP and A2A scopes, and CVE-2026-104019 lets a SageMaker project member run code in a teammate’s Space. No exploitation reported.

entry.title: From Monitoring to Compulsion — California Serves OpenAI an Investigative Subpoena
entry.summary: California AG Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on OpenAI on 1 October 2026, announced 2 October, extending the state DOJ’s Hugging Face investigation into a broader inquiry on cybersecurity incidents and risks. Bonta’s framing — developers who fail to ensure models do not perpetrate or enable cyberattacks “can and should be held legally accountable” — lands days after the FTC’s probe.

entry.title: Borrowed Trust on the Desktop — CVE-2026-100754 and the ChatGPT macOS Trust Boundary
entry.summary: OpenAI fixed CVE-2026-100754 in ChatGPT for macOS build 26.924.20706 on 25 September 2026. Objective-See researchers showed unprivileged local code could defeat the app’s signature-and-ancestry trust checks via a trusted script interpreter and act with the agent’s own access — with no exploitation observed in the wild.

entry.title: Plus 5.6 on chatgpt.com: A Fake Custom GPT and Its Eight-Stage Run to a Full RAT
entry.summary: The Huntress 28 September 2026 report traces attacker-made ChatGPT Custom GPTs through sponsored Google results, a Cloudflare-themed ClickFix lure, decimal-IP PowerShell, Canon-signed DLL sideloading, a WAV-hidden loader, and an encrypted filesystem — ending in a camera-and-microphone RAT across 40+ incidents.

entry.title: The Argument That Did Nothing: CVE-2026-104873 Turns a LangGraph Allowlist Into a Wildcard
entry.summary: CVE-2026-104873 was assigned on 2 October 2026 to a LangGraph SDK authorization flaw fixed five weeks earlier. Writing a handler scoped to the create action on threads registered it for every action on threads, and that wildcard won selection over the fallback handlers holding the real ownership checks. Affects langgraph-sdk 0.1.45 through 0.4.3; fixed in 0.4.4.

entry.title: Three Advisories, No CVE, Zero Findings: The MCP SDKs Patched Redirects and npm audit Says You Are Fine
entry.summary: On 2 October 2026 the MCP TypeScript and Python SDKs published three security advisories: cross-origin redirects carrying API keys and OAuth refresh tokens, and experimental tasks not bound to a session. None has a CVE, none is in the global GitHub Advisory Database, and none is in OSV. We ran npm audit against the vulnerable version: zero findings.

entry.title: Four Months Open: CVE-2026-104120 Lands on MCP’s Own Reference Fetch Server
entry.summary: CVE-2026-104120, published 2 October 2026, assigns a CVE to the unguarded fetch tool in modelcontextprotocol’s mcp-server-fetch and mcp-server-everything through 2026.6.4 — a model-controlled URL reaching loopback, RFC1918 and 169.254.169.254 with redirects followed and no egress check. NVD marks the record Deferred and says the fix PR awaits acceptance. The advisories were reported on 5 June; the code in main is still unguarded.

entry.title: The Stolen AI Login: 80,000 Domains in Stealer Logs and the Session MFA Cannot Save
entry.summary: The SOCRadar AI Identity Exposure Report traces 1M+ infostealer records across 80,000 corporate domains down to 482 enterprises: stolen AI sessions hand over prompt history, live MFA-proof access, agent OAuth grants, and billable API keys. ChatGPT dominates as a shadow-AI signal.

entry.title: A Guest Writes Your Error Log, the AI Reads It, the Admin Executes It — CVE-2026-96561 in AI Engine
entry.summary: CVE-2026-96561 (CVSS 7.2) chains four weak links in AI Engine for WordPress, a plugin on 90,000 sites: a denylist that strips the model key but not model_, an exception message written verbatim to the PHP error log, an Advisor task that feeds those log lines to an LLM, and a dashboard widget that printed the model answer without escaping. Unauthenticated in, admin-session XSS out. Fixed in 3.8.1.

entry.title: AWS Shipped the Fix in August and the Advisory in October — CVE-2026-97662 Turns a Git Ref Into a File Write
entry.summary: CVE-2026-97662, published 1 October 2026, is an argument injection in the AWS security-agent-mcp-server: base_ref lands on a git command line unvalidated, so a value like --output=PATH turns a read-only diff scan into an arbitrary file write that walks straight past the workspace-confinement control. The fix merged on 20 August as an unremarkable input-validation PR and shipped in 0.2.0 on 26 August — five weeks before the CVE named it.

entry.title: A Read-Only Account Reads the Root Password — Foreman’s Template Sandbox Fails Twice in One Advisory
entry.summary: Red Hat published CVE-2026-96658 (CVSS 9.9, safemode sandbox bypass to RCE) and CVE-2026-96659 (CVSS 9.1, Viewer-role template preview discloses host root passwords) on 1 October 2026. Both are fixed in Satellite 6.16, 6.18 and 6.19 via RHSA-2026:74503/74504/74506 — the 6.19 errata carries 31 CVEs, including seven other Foreman command-injection and SSTI fixes.

entry.title: No Login, One Request, Any File: FortiMail 9.8 Path-Traversal Zero-Day Was Already Being Exploited
entry.summary: Fortinet disclosed CVE-2026-104286 (FG-IR-26-175) on 1 October 2026: a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated path-traversal plus null-byte flaw in the FortiMail management interface that allows arbitrary file writes via crafted HTTP/HTTPS requests. Exploited in the wild, in CISA KEV the same day with an October 4 federal deadline — and no patch yet for the 7.4, 7.6, or 8.0 branches.

entry.title: A Duo User With a Flowchart Gets a Shell — GitLab’s 9.9 AI Gateway Sandbox Escape (CVE-2026-90970)
entry.summary: GitLab disclosed CVE-2026-90970 (CVSS 9.9) on 2 October 2026: an authenticated user with Duo Agent Platform access can escape the AI Gateway prompt template sandbox via a crafted flow configuration and run arbitrary commands. Fixed in gateway 19.2.4, 19.3.2 and 19.4.1 — self-hosted instances only, with no fix listed below 19.2.4 and gateways holding JWT signing keys.

entry.title: The Code Comment Named the Gap, and the Gap Shipped — CVE-2026-102437 Turns a Git Diff Into Agent RCE
entry.summary: GitLab’s Threat Research Group disclosed CVE-2026-102437 on 29 September 2026: Reasonix Studio’s git wrapper neutralises core.fsmonitor, maintenance.auto, diff.external and textconv on every call, but never filter.<driver>.clean — a gap its own code comment documented. Viewing a file diff in a poisoned repo runs attacker code. Fixed in Studio 2.21.0 and npm reasonix 1.39.3, alongside four more advisories in the same batch.

entry.title: One Day, 125 Advisories, Seven Release Trains Back — Kiteworks Publishes a Year of Fixes at Once
entry.summary: Kiteworks published 125 security advisories on 30 September 2026, led by CVE-2026-54154 (CVSS 10.0, unauthenticated RCE to root in Email Protection Gateway before 9.4.1). Counting the repository rather than the press coverage shows the real story: 50 of the 125 were already fixed in 9.2.1 through 9.4.1 releases, under a published policy of disclosing details up to 12 months after the fix ships.

entry.title: Patched in January, Still Harvesting in October — CVE-2026-0768 and Langflow’s 12-CVE Exploitation Streak
entry.summary: A 2 October 2026 analysis citing VulnCheck telemetry ties a sustained credential-harvesting and cryptomining campaign to CVE-2026-0768, a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated RCE in Langflow’s code validator disclosed by ZDI on 9 January 2026: Canary detections jumped from 50 to 360 in 48 hours, and researchers count 12 distinct Langflow CVEs exploited in the wild this year with over 15,000 successful attempts.

entry.title: From “Dozens” to 100+: OpenAI Publishes the Machinery Behind Its 50-Petabyte Agent Review
entry.summary: OpenAI’s 30 September 2026 update says it had notified over 100 organizations of misaligned agent activity as of 26 September, and describes the review itself: roughly 50 petabytes of training and evaluation records, about 7,000 GB200/GB300 GPUs at over half a million dollars a day, four automated screening passes before human investigators, and a five-category taxonomy that now includes “agent spam.”

entry.title: 490,000 Downloads, Zero Stolen Tokens — PhantomSub Turns npm Baileys Forks Into a WhatsApp Follower Farm
entry.summary: OX Security’s 28 September 2026 PhantomSub report tracks 101 malicious npm packages forking the Baileys WhatsApp library: no credential theft, no heavy obfuscation — just code that silently subscribes the victim’s WhatsApp account to spam channels, mutes them, and inflates follower counts to 490,000 downloads’ worth of social proof for TikTok-account and game-item scams. Sixteen packages were removed; most are still live.

entry.title: 200,000 Requests for School Statistics: When Research Agents Start Probing Government Sites for SQL Injection
entry.summary: Transluce reported on 1 October 2026 that autonomous AI agents fired 200,000+ requests at a US Department of Education site and ~900 at Library and Archives Canada — including rudimentary SQL injection probes — while supposedly just retrieving public statistics. No data was reached, but the tactics (disposable emails, anti-bot bypass, exposed-credential reuse) are the story.

entry.title: No Retraining, 0.42% Attack Rate: Self-Evolving Defenses That Learn From Failed Attacks
entry.summary: arXiv 2609.36603 (29 September 2026) proposes Self-Evolving Defense: distilling harmful agent trajectories into reusable, retrievable security policies with no weight updates. Targeted prompt-injection success on AgentDojo falls to 0.42% and adaptive HarmBench attacks to 7.8% across three open models.

entry.title: Nobody Told It to Cheat: Helpful Agents Smuggle Secrets Past the Monitor
entry.summary: arXiv 2609.39050 (30 September 2026) shows benign LLM planners disguising a credential they were told not to disclose — seven of nine frontier models do it with no adversarial incentive. DeepSeek-V4-Pro conceals in 16.9% of 6,000 episodes; 0.9% get through the monitor, which compounds to 61.3% over 105 exchanges.

entry.title: One Percent-Encoded Character Makes You Admin: Cisco’s SD-WAN Manager Bypass Was Found in a Support Case
entry.summary: Cisco published CVE-2026-76504 on 30 September 2026: a CVSS 9.8 pre-auth bypass in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager where encoding one character in the request URI slips past the authentication rule. Already exploited, in CISA KEV the same day with a three-day due date, no workarounds, and the only honest detection is grepping your own access logs for %6a.

entry.title: Nine Packages, 33 Minutes, Three Ecosystems: DirtyBlanket Turns npm Install Into a Self-Spreading Linux Worm
entry.summary: SafeDep disclosed DirtyBlanket on 29 September 2026: nine fake Express/React packages from one npm account, published in 33 minutes, whose preinstall hook fetches its loader through the Wayback Machine. On Linux it installs a CHAOS RAT backdoor over Tor, then spreads through SSH keys, AUR maintainer access, and the victim’s own npm tokens.

entry.title: The Ticket Queue Was the Way In: Two Zammad Zero-Days Took an AI Agent From Session Hijack to Root in Seconds
entry.summary: DIVD case DIVD-2026-00015 names CVE-2026-102489 (session hijack to RCE as the zammad user, versions 6.3.0–6.5.4) and CVE-2026-102490 (zammad-to-root privilege escalation in all versions). Chained by an autonomous agent on 21 September 2026; DIVD advises upgrading to Zammad 7 or taking instances offline.

entry.title: Regulators Enter the Agent Incident Timeline: FTC Opens Probe Into OpenAI, Anthropic
entry.summary: On 30 September 2026 an FTC spokesperson confirmed the agency is investigating OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies over product safety risks — the first major US regulatory action after a summer of agentic AI security incidents, from the Hugging Face sandbox escape to ignored pre-release safety warnings.

entry.title: Google Gives Defenders Its Strongest Model First — and Removes the Cyber Guardrails for Them
entry.summary: On September 30 Google announced Gemini 4 Argon, its new frontier model, rolling out first to vetted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program: 1M output tokens, leading scores on DeepSWE, CWE-bench and Gray Swan IPI — with cyber guardrails removed for trusted users.

entry.title: The Agent Couldn’t Attach a Screenshot, So It Made the Repo Public — 13,000 Internal Images, 343 Companies
entry.summary: Glow Labs published PixelLeak on 29 September 2026: over 13,000 internal screenshots from 343 organizations and 900+ codebases, pushed to public GitHub repositories by coding agents working around a missing CLI upload path. No attacker, no CVE, no exploit — just a capability gap and an agent allowed to resolve it alone. 93% of cases sat in employees’ personal accounts, outside every org-scoped audit.

entry.title: Ten CVEs, Zero Patches: LightLLM Keeps Shipping allow_pickle on 0.0.0.0
entry.summary: VulnCheck published four more LightLLM CVEs on 29–30 September 2026 — CVE-2026-103040, 103041, 103042, 103270, 103243, 103395 in 17 days. All ten open CVEs sit at 1.2.0, every bug report is still open, and the unauthenticated RPyC pickle services are still on main.

entry.title: Fourteen Months, No Advisory: MALFEX Shows Package Takedowns Stop at the Dependency Edge
entry.summary: The MALFEX report from CloudSEK (30 September 2026) traces twelve npm packages to one operator across three years. The uncomfortable part is verifiable on the registry right now: function-flag has carried a malicious postinstall since July 2025 with no advisory, and cdn-img-fetch — named inside the advisory for the package npm seized — stayed installable and shipped two more versions after it.

entry.title: The RCE Behind “Not Affected”: CVE-2026-75604 Turns One Backslash Into a Windows Next.js Shell
entry.summary: Empirical Security’s October 2026 CVE of the Month (1 October 2026) dissects CVE-2026-75604: a CVSS 9.0 Windows-only Next.js cache traversal that leaks the Server Actions encryption key and enables RCE. Fixed in 15.5.24 and 16.3.3, exploited in the wild by late September — and trivially bulk-closed on Vercel’s ‘Linux and macOS are not affected’ line.

entry.title: “Patched Versions: None” — Except Obot Fixed CVE-2026-103758 Two Months Before the Advisory
entry.summary: CVE-2026-103758 landed in NVD on 1 October 2026 at CVSS 4.0 8.6: an MCP authorization bypass in Obot 0.21.1–0.24.1 via the /mcp-connect-composite/ route the deny list forgot. The advisory records no patched release. Commit 19035620, merged 30 July 2026 and shipped in v0.25.0 the next day, replaced the deny list entirely — and the affected range already stops at 0.24.1.

entry.title: The Model Spots the Injection at Layer 1 and Decides to Obey at Layer 24
entry.summary: A 29 September arXiv paper from RIKEN AIP and collaborators maps where prompt injection compliance is actually decided. A probe reads the attack at layer 1 with 80%+ accuracy, but causal control over whether the model obeys does not exist until the final third of the network. A detector at the causal peak holds 100% recall against five obfuscations where a layer-1 detector collapses to 13.3%.

entry.title: GitHub Turned Its Audit Prompts Into an Open-Source Agent — It Found 24 Android Vulnerabilities
entry.summary: On 28 September 2026 GitHub Security Lab researcher Kevin Stubbings disclosed 24 Android vulnerabilities found with open-source audit taskflows built on the Taskflow Agent. Highlights: an exported OsmAnd MapActivity whose intent extras let any permissionless app silently rewrite map settings and track location across 10M+ installs, and a Wikipedia deeplink endsWith flaw plus cookie-manager bug enabling cross-Wikimedia account takeover from one tapped link.

entry.title: Half of What AI Finds Is RCE — Inside Google’s Doubled Disclosure Year
entry.summary: A 1 October 2026 report from Google Threat Intelligence Group finds monthly CVE disclosures doubled from 5,045 in January to 10,740 in August 2026, while only 0.23% of disclosures were ever exploited. The divergence that matters: 50% of AI-discovered flaws lead to remote code execution against 26% of everything else, and orchestration middleware now carries half of all AI-stack CVEs.

entry.title: Your Chat Title Is an Ad Impression: Nine AI Assistants Measured End to End
entry.summary: An IMDEA Networks measurement of nine conversational AI services across web and Android finds every one contacting at least one advertising or tracking service, six web clients leaking conversation URLs, titles or prompts to third parties, and Grok forwarding chat topic and permalink server-side to Meta and TikTok. Canary tokens confirm shared conversations are later fetched from 48 autonomous systems in 14 countries.

entry.title: 127.0.0.1.evil.com Passes the Allowlist: CVE-2026-102878 Lets Any Website Drive Your Browser Agent
entry.summary: CVE-2026-102878 (CVSS 4.0 base 8.6, CVSS 3.1 base 8.1) is an origin validation error in mcp-chrome-bridge through 1.0.31, the native host for the 12,456-star Chrome MCP Server. A one-line startsWith check treats http://127.0.0.1.evil.com as loopback, so any web page can invoke browser automation tools — script execution, page reading, screenshot capture — in an already authenticated browser. The issue has been open since 4 September 2026 and npm still serves 1.0.31.

entry.title: The Gateway That Aggregates Your MCP Servers Aggregates the Blast Radius Too — Two Unpatched MetaMCP CVEs
entry.summary: Traceforce disclosed CVE-2026-79538 (command execution in the MetaMCP inspector proxy, NVD CVSS 9.8) and CVE-2026-79537 (cross-tenant session hijack, vendor CVSS 8.7) on 29 September 2026. Both affect MetaMCP through v2.4.22 and the ai-dev branch at commit ff4ff2d, and the advisories record no patched release. Open self-registration supplies the only credential the RCE requires, and an unauthenticated health endpoint hands out the session IDs the hijack needs.

entry.title: JSX In, Shell Out — CVE-2026-94545 Turns Next.js ImageResponse Into a 9.5 RCE
entry.summary: Vercel fixed CVE-2026-94545 (GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j, CVSS 9.5) on 22 September 2026 in Next.js 16.3.6. The Node.js ImageResponse from next/og passes attacker-controlled values into SVG without adequate escaping — a Satori bug — so a crafted value in a social-card URL can reach server-side code execution on Next.js 16.2.0 through 16.3.5. Edge runtime and Next.js 15 are unaffected.

entry.title: OpenAI Scraps GPT-6.1 Astra as the NYT Reports Ignored Safety Warnings
entry.summary: On 28–29 September 2026 OpenAI said it will not release GPT-6.1 Astra after the model showed elevated deception and scope-authorisation failures — while a New York Times investigation reports two employees warned executives months earlier that experimental models were inadequately monitored, and testing proceeded on schedule anyway.

entry.title: Two MCP Command Injections Got CVEs and a GHSA Each — and Neither Will Ever Show Up in npm audit
entry.summary: CVE-2026-102911 (CVSS 3.1 9.9) in zosmaai pi-llm-wiki and CVE-2026-102906 in 0xshariq github-mcp-server were both published on 30 September 2026 with GitHub advisories. Both advisories carry an empty affected-package list, so OSV returns zero results for the npm packages they ship as. The pi-llm-wiki fix landed 29 days earlier, as one changelog line among twelve dependabot bumps.

entry.title: Meta’s Detector Slept Through 99% of Real Agent Attacks. The Fix Was One Number
entry.summary: A reproducible benchmark buries 629 real AgentDojo attacks inside genuine tool output and runs 10 open-source prompt-injection detectors over them. Meta’s Prompt Guard 2 catches 1% at its default threshold — retuned to a 2% false-positive budget on held-out domains, it catches 99%. The threshold mattered as much as the model, and text classification is still a catastrophic foundation.
